https://telex.hu/sport/2026/09/21/mlsz-m.text: Menü Kereső Nehéz helyzetben a magyar futballválogatott: Varga Barnabás és Sallai Roland is megsérült Sport Pál Tamás Állítsd be a Telexet megbízható forrásnak! Beállítom Sérülés miatt Varga Barnabás, Sallai Roland és Callum Styles sem csatlakozik a magyar futballválogatott Nemzetek Ligája-mérkőzésekre készülő keretéhez – írta az MTI. A Magyar Labdarúgó Szövetség vasárnap közölte , hogy combsérülést szenvedett a görög bajnok AEK Athén magyar válogatott csatára, Varga Barnabás. A helyére Marco Rossi szövetségi kapitány a holland ADO Den Haagban játszó Bárány Donátot hívta be a keretbe. A 26 éves Bárány korábban kétszer játszott a válogatottban , idén nyáron igazolt a Debrecenből Hollandiába. Az új klubjában múlt héten szerezte meg az első gólját a Cambuur elleni bajnokin. Hétfőn aztán újabb sérülésekről számolt be az MLSZ: a török a Galatasarayban játszó Sallai, valamint az angol másodosztályú West Bromwich Albionban futballozó Styles is megsérült, így ők sem állnak Marco Rossi rendelkezésére. A szövetségi kapitány a Puskás Akadémiából Nagy Zsoltot és a Vasasból az újonc Tóth Milánt hívta be a pótlásukra. A keret tagjai hétfőn találkoznak Telkiben. A magyar válogatott szeptember 25-én Ukrajnát, október 2-án Grúziát fogadja a Puskás Arénában, szeptember 28-án Belfastban Észak-Írország, október 5-én pedig a szlovákiai Nagyszombatban (Trnava) Ukrajna ellen lép pályára a Nemzetek Ligája másodosztályát jelentő B divízióban. A négyesből az első feljut, az utolsó kiesik, a második a feljutásért, a harmadik pedig a bennmaradásért játszik osztályozót. Kedvenceink Partnereinktől Állítsd be a Telexet megbízható forrásnak! Photograph: ZUMA Press, Inc./Alamy View image in fullscreen OpenAI CEO Sam Altman. The company said it would resume training its latest models ‘only when we are confident that we have addition safeguards’. Photograph: ZUMA Press, Inc./Alamy OpenAI OpenAI halts training of latest models as reports mount of AI agents going rogue Decision follows disclosures that OpenAI agents searching government websites had acted in unexpected ways Associated Press Sat 26 Sep 2026 21.10 EDT Last modified on Sat 26 Sep 2026 22.33 EDT Share Prefer the Guardian on Google OpenAI said it has paused training of its latest artificial intelligence models as reports of AI agents going rogue mount. The decision to halt development came just hours after the company disclosed Friday that it was reviewing several incidents from the summer in which OpenAI agents searching federal government websites acted in unexpected ways beyond what was asked of them while gathering and distributing information. Separately, the AI evaluator Transluce said agents that appeared to come from OpenAI tried unsuccessfully to hack into a US Department of Education website, a detail that OpenAI has not confirmed. OpenAI said in a statement that it will resume training “only when we are confident that we have additional safeguards” in place, adding that it expects it will have to “hit pause” again as AI develops and other issues emerge. Last week Australia’s prime minister, Anthony Albanese, revealed an OpenAI agent had breached the government’s national healthcare system – but said no sensitive information had been compromised. AI labs are facing pressure from lawmakers and tech experts to slow development so they can build guardrails to stop agents from acting on their own, hacking websites and disclosing nonpublic information. The heads of both OpenAI and rival Anthropic have called for a slowdown too. OpenAI hack on Australian government reveals anxiety at heart of global artificial intelligence dilemma Read more It is the second time in three months that OpenAI has halted development of its models. The first came in July after disclosure of a cyber-attack targeting AI startup Hugging Face , a now notorious incident that raised fears the industry was losing control. In a meeting with Chinese president Xi Jinping this week, Donald Trump agreed to share information on AI dangers and coordinate efforts to keep it safe. Trump believes AI fears are overblown, though, and later suggested that he plans no crackdown of his own. The US is not going to be “putting on brakes”, Trump told reporters outside the White House. “They want to stop our progress because we’re leading China by a lot, and we’re going to keep it that way.” The latest OpenAI incidents did not appear to involve the disclosure of any nonpublic information but were concerning enough for the company to warn the federal agencies involved. In the education department incident, OpenAI agents found API “developer keys” to access government data, though ultimately only publicly available information was gathered. In another case involving the securities and exchange commission, agents found information freely available to all but then posted it elsewhere on the internet, an act that went beyond what they were instructed to do. US Securities and Exchange Commission spokesperson Kurt Hopfenspirger said on Saturday that “no nonpublic information was accessed”. The Department of Education said earlier that it found “no evidence of any impact to our website or databases”. Several other AI companies have disclosed incidents of their models going rogue and even hacking websites. OpenAI’s CEO, Sam Altman, said in a social media post on Friday that the Hugging Face incident “is still the most severe event we’ve seen”. OpenAI previously shared six other reports of “unexpected or concerning” behaviour in AI models and introduced a framework for tracking, probing and disclosing instances. https://www.politico.eu/article/zelensky.text: ABU DHABI — Ukraine’s President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said European countries supporting his cause must decide fast who will represent them in peace talks. That means ideally one person should have a mandate from the EU and other non-EU countries who have backed Ukraine, such as the U.K. and Norway, because “unity” is important, he suggested. “I think that in November, not later, we need to accept who will represent Europe in negotiations,” he said. “It will be better because they will get [a] mandate for negotiations and they will get a mandate from all Europe, all this coalition.” Advertisement Advertisement With Europe set to take on a more important role in talks with Russia and the United States, Zelenskyy’s comments join a growing chorus of demands for the EU and others to unite behind one top negotiator or a small team at the highest level. Speaking to reporters during his trip to Denmark on Tuesday, the Ukrainian leader said he wanted a “dialogue” with the EU and other European powers over who will represent them. He said it would be “better” this way, rather than just presenting their answer to Ukraine, which is “not good, really.” “I hope that not later than the end of November — better in Germany on 19th [at a Coalition of the Willing meeting] — fix it. We will see.” Europe has been struggling to work out a plan for how to engage in top-level dialogue with Moscow and Washington over ending the war in Ukraine. Despite providing most of the foreign financing for Ukraine’s war effort, EU countries have been split over who should represent them, or whether they should be talking to Russian leader Vladimir Putin at all. Italian Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni last week blasted the European Union’s engagement with the peace talks as “all over the place.” Leaders are due to grapple with these questions at a summit in Dublin later this week. As talks with Ukraine, Russia and the U.S. resumed in Abu Dhabi on Tuesday, American officials made clear they wanted Europe fully at the table next time the negotiations take place. That is partly because the U.S. wants to bring a review of wider European security arrangements for Europe into the negotiations over peace in Ukraine — a longstanding Russian demand.
